Van Eyk explained that her first reaction when she received a call from the school was one of concern rather than of excitement, thinking that there could be some problem with her own child before finding out the real reason for the phone call. She then went on to say that she found the whole event unforgettable, especially since it was a child attending the same school that found the bottle.For an area such as Belle River, which is part of the Municipality of Lakeshore and is inhabited by about ten thousand people, calculating the probability of finding the closed bottle in the same vicinity where it was dumped, with the possibility that it would then pass to the same school’s student, is quite hard to estimate. St. Pierre, commenting on the results of the situation, noted that the bottle might simply go unnoticed indefinitely or be found by a person who had no relation to the school whatsoever. However, a letter written by one nine-year-old girl in 1998 was eventually read in front of a class that also included her nine-year-old daughter in 2024.
Article Summary: Makenzie Morris, now known as Scarlet Van Eyk, was a fourth-grader at St. John the Baptist Catholic Elementary School in Belle River, Ontario in 1998. She typed out a letter about the waters of the Great Lakes on a computer in her classroom as part of a class assignment. She sealed it in a plastic bottle with wax and threw it in Lake St. Clair. In the fall of 2024, a kindergartner from the same school found the bottle and took it to the school. Makenzie's own daughter, Scarlet, was in the same class at the time.

Article Title: In 1873, Andrew Hallidie tested San Francisco’s first cable car on Clay Street, creating a new way to travel up the city’s steep hills without horses
Article Text:
PC: Cable Car Heritage Museum

How the San Francisco cable car climbed steep hills without horses

How the 1873 Clay Street cable car covered a 5,197-foot steep incline

San Francisco’s cable car system expanded to 53 miles by 1883

PC: Cable Car Heritage Museum

In August 1873, San Francisco tested a new cable railway system designed to operate on streets where horses struggled with steep grades. Andrew Smith Hallidie tested the first cable car on Clay Street on 2 August, using an endless wire rope placed in a tube below the surface of the street. The Clay Street Hill Railroad began public service on 1 September 1873. Its route climbed a hill rising 307 feet above Kearny Street, with the steepest grade recorded as 1 in 6 15/100. The cable system later spread across San Francisco, while cable cars continued serving steep hills as electric streetcars and buses expanded.According to the Cable Car Heritage Museum, a contemporary description by A. S. Hallidie, reproduced by the system, was designed for streets “so steep as to make the use of horses difficult or impossible”. It used an “endless wire rope placed in a tube below the surface of the ground, between the tracks of a railroad”. A stationary engine kept the rope moving, while a gripping mechanism connected the moving rope to the cars above the street.The rope was contained in iron tubes and moved over sheaves along the route. A slot in the upper side of the tube allowed the gripping attachment from the car to reach the moving rope below the street.The grip could be engaged or released by the person operating the car, allowing the vehicle to move with the cable or stop when the rope was released. The source also states that the car could be started more smoothly than by horses and stopped on the road.The Cable Car Museum's reproduced description records that the Clay Street route began at the intersection of Kearny and Clay streets. The summit was 307 feet above Kearny Street, while the incline on Clay Street had double track and measured 5,197 feet in length. The source records a series of ascending and descending grades along the route, with the steepest grade listed as 1 in 6 15/100.The cable system itself used an endless steel wire rope three inches in circumference and 11,000 feet long. It was placed in iron tubes supported by sheaves, while an engine at the engine house drove the grip pulleys that moved the rope. The source states that the rope operated for 17½ hours a day at a speed of six miles per hour, with cars starting every five minutes except in the afternoon, when they started every three minutes.The Clay Street Hill Railroad was the only cable car company in San Francisco for four years. The Sutter Street Railroad developed its own version of Hallidie's patented system and began cable service in 1877. Other companies followed, in including the California Street Cable Railroad in 1878, the Geary Street, Park & Ocean Railroad in 1880, the Presidio & Ferries Railroad in 1882, the Market Street Cable Railway in 1883, the Ferries & Cliff House Railway in 1888 and the Omnibus Railroad & Cable Company in 1889. The museum states that San Francisco companies eventually laid 53 miles of track extending from the Ferry Building to the Presidio, Golden Gate Park, the Castro and the Mission.Electric streetcars later became the preferred form of city transit because they required only half the investment to build and maintain, could reach more areas and were quicker. However, cable cars remained capable of travelling over San Francisco's steep hills, and some lines were rebuilt. By 1947, the lower operating costs of buses led Mayor Lapham to call for the removal of the cable car lines. A public campaign led by Friedel Klussmann and the Citizens' Committee to Save the Cable Cars resulted in Measure 10, which passed and ordered the city to maintain the Powell Street cable car system.
Article Summary: The Clay Street Hill Railroad began public service on 1 September 1873. Its route climbed a hill rising 307 feet above Kearny Street, with the steepest grade recorded as 1 in 6 15/100. The cable system later spread across San Francisco, while cable cars continued serving steep hills as electric streetcars and buses expanded.

Article Title: Two sold-out Ed Sheeran concerts at Massachusetts’ Gillette Stadium were canceled hours before the weekend shows; the venue cited severe nor’easter warnings, with fans promised refunds as the storm th
Article Text: Ed Sheeran’s two sold-out concerts at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, were canceled just hours before the scheduled performances as a powerful nor’easter threatened New England. The cancellation was reported by the BBC, CBS Boston and Boston 25 News, with the venue and tour promoter pointing to severe weather conditions and safety concerns. The shows, scheduled for Friday, September 25, and Saturday, September 26, were part of Sheeran’s ongoing Loop Tour. Both dates were listed as canceled on Ticketmaster, with the concerts originally scheduled to begin at 8 p.m.The decision came as a major fall nor’easter moved toward the region, bringing the threat of heavy rain, strong winds, coastal flooding and rough surf across parts of New England. Local weather warnings remained in effect through the weekend, prompting concerns about travel as well as conditions at the outdoor stadium.Gillette Stadium said the decision followed consultations with local officials, the promoter and the tour. The venue said safety was the priority and confirmed that refunds would be available through the original point of purchase. Fans who bought their tickets through Ticketmaster were set to receive automatic refunds.The abrupt cancellation marked another disruption for Sheeran’s US tour, which has already faced significant attention in recent weeks over the removal of rapper Macklemore as an opening act.Macklemore had performed on earlier dates of the tour while making outspoken comments supporting Palestinians and calling for a ceasefire in Gaza. Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and operator of Gillette Stadium, had objected to Macklemore’s appearances following those comments. The rapper was subsequently removed from the remaining tour dates, with the promoter saying venue owners would not allow him to perform. Sheeran has said the decision was made by his promoter rather than by him.The controversy also prompted several artists connected with the tour to withdraw. Sheeran returned to the stage in Philadelphia on September 19 with a new backing lineup and addressed the turmoil surrounding the tour. The Massachusetts shows were therefore already among the most closely watched dates on the Loop Tour. Their cancellation, however, was officially attributed to the weather rather than the earlier dispute.For ticket holders, the immediate concern was whether they would be able to recover the money spent on the canceled performances. The stadium confirmed that refunds were available, while Ticketmaster’s event listings now show both September 25 and September 26 performances as canceled.Sheeran’s next listed US performances are scheduled to continue in October, with dates at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta on October 3 and Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on October 10.
Article Summary: Ed Sheeran's two sold-out concerts at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, were canceled just hours before the scheduled performances. The cancellation was reported by the BBC, CBS Boston and Boston 25 News, with the venue and tour promoter pointing to severe weather conditions and safety concerns. The shows were scheduled for Friday, September 25, and Saturday, September 26.

Article Title: Meet Jawad Khalfan, the Long Island entrepreneur who started a security company from a garage in 2020; six years later, SecureTech Systems has completed more than 1,500 installations and won a 2026 st
Article Text: A small security business launched in 2020 has grown into a Long Island technology company with more than 1,500 installations to its name. SecureTech Systems, co-founded by Jawad Khalfan, was recently recognised as the 2026 Next-Gen Entrepreneur of the Year by the New York Small Business Development Centers (New York SBDC). The award was announced as part of the organisation’s statewide client awards programme, which selected recipients from more than 27,000 small-business clients. The New York SBDC, SecureTech Systems and industry publication SDM Magazine provide details about the company’s growth, services and evolution from residential work towards larger commercial projects.Khalfan launched SecureTech Systems in April 2020 with business partner Joseph Kessler. In a 2025 account of the company’s fifth anniversary, Khalfan described the early years as a period of uncertainty and persistence, with the business having initially operated from a much smaller setup before developing into an established company. The Better Business Bureau lists SecureTech Systems as having been incorporated on April 9, 2020, with Khalfan as CEO and co-founder.Today, SecureTech operates from Garden City South, New York, and works as a low-voltage technology integrator rather than simply an alarm installer.Its services cover areas including video surveillance, access control, networking, audio-visual systems and other integrated security technologies. The company says its work spans commercial buildings, schools, healthcare facilities, managed properties and other institutional environments.One of the biggest changes in the company’s trajectory has been its move towards commercial security. The New York SBDC’s account of the award notes that SecureTech initially had a heavier focus on residential projects before Khalfan shifted the company’s attention towards commercial installations and larger opportunities. That change has helped shape the type of work the company takes on today. (LinkedIn⁠ )The shift can be seen in SecureTech’s work with educational institutions. A case study published by security technology manufacturer AtlasIED details a Long Island school project involving surveillance cameras, card access control, networking upgrades, low-voltage cabling and a mass-notification system. More than 80 classrooms received new communication equipment as part of the upgrade, illustrating the broader range of technology involved in modern security projects.The company has also accumulated recognition before its latest state award. Khalfan was named to Long Island Business News’ 30 Under 30 list in 2023, while SecureTech Systems has also been recognised in connection with business and entrepreneurship programmes. Its own awards record lists a 2023 Rising Star Under 30 recognition, a 2024 Rookie of the Year finalist position and a 2024 Diversity in Business award for Khalfan.The 2026 New York SBDC award adds another milestone to that progression. SecureTech Systems was scheduled for its Next-Gen Entrepreneur of the Year celebration on September 16, with the Long Island SBDC at Stony Brook University supporting the business and Robert B. Harrison serving as its business adviser. The recognition comes six years after the company was established and follows its expansion from a small startup into a business reporting more than 1,500 completed installations.For Khalfan, the story of SecureTech Systems is ultimately tied to a change in scale as much as a change in technology: a business that began during a difficult economic period has gradually moved towards larger commercial projects, more sophisticated security systems and a broader role as a technology partner for organisations across Long Island and the wider New York area.
Article Summary: Jawad Khalfan launched SecureTech Systems in April 2020. The company has more than 1,500 installations to its name. It works as a low-voltage technology integrator rather than an alarm installer. Its services cover areas including video surveillance, access control, networking, audio-visual systems and other integrated security technologies.

Article Title: 15 years ago, a Colorado couple bought a battered ranch; they now turned its damaged landscape into a wildlife-friendly working ranch
Article Text:
Eagle Rock Ranch of Park County has been selected as the recipient of the 2026 Colorado Leopold Conservation Award. Image Credit: Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust

How did the damaged Eagle Rock Ranch begin its transformation

Major changes that helped in recovering the land

How is wildlife benefiting from the ranch’s changes

Ranch’s work extend beyond its own boundaries

Ranch and its wider wildlife community

Years of conservation work bring Eagle Rock Ranch a major award

Eagle Rock Ranch in Colorado’s Park County has undergone a major transformation since Dave and Jeannie Gottenborg took ownership of the property. What they inherited was a badly damaged working ranch, with muddy corrals, cut creekside willows, worn-out fencing and hay fields managed in ways that harmed wildlife, soil and water. Over the years, the couple began repairing the land while continuing to run cattle, gradually changing how the ranch handled water, grazing, vegetation and wildlife. Their work has now earned Eagle Rock Ranch the 2026 Colorado Leopold Conservation Award, recognising its approach to conservation.According to the Sand County Foundation , the Gottenborgs became owners of Eagle Rock Ranch about 15 years before the 2026 award. The property was described as a wounded landscape, with corrals that were knee-deep in mud and manure. Creekside willows had been removed to make room for more hay, while hay fields were repeatedly mowed close to the ground.Those practices created problems beyond the appearance of the ranch. The Sand County Foundation says they were detrimental to wildlife, soil health and water quality. Fences were also regularly damaged by migrating elk, despite earlier attempts to keep the animals away using propane cannons.The condition of the property meant the new owners had to address basic problems before building a more sustainable system. They removed rubbish and rotting corrals and began restoring vegetation with native grasses. Old, rusty barbed wire was replaced with fencing designed to be safer for wildlife.One of the changes involved the way hay fields were managed. Instead of cutting the vegetation completely short, the ranch leaves enough hay stubble standing to trap blowing snow. According to the Sand County Foundation, this also helps in slowing down erosion and allows more water to enter the soil, improving its condition.Water management was also redesigned. Clean water from a settling pond is now carried to the hay fields through an underground culvert system. A solar-powered pump supplies fresh drinking water through miles of underground pipe to 10 stock tanks.The positioning of those tanks has allowed the Gottenborgs to use rotational grazing. Rather than concentrating cattle in the same areas, the system helps spread grazing pressure across the ranch. The Sand County Foundation says this increases forage availability while reducing the impact of livestock on the land.The restoration has also reached the ranch’s creek and surrounding habitat. The Sand County Foundation reports that the creek now runs clean and supports abundant fish following erosion-control work and the addition of fish habitat structures.Hundreds of willow saplings have been planted along the waterway. They help hold the soil in place while providing shade for trout. The ranch has also installed screens on irrigation ditches to stop fish from entering them, while fish ladders give trout better access to spawning areas.Wildlife protection extends beyond the water. Every stock tank has a ladder intended to prevent birds from drowning. Bird houses were installed to encourage Mountain Bluebirds to return, while bat houses provide places for bats that can contribute to pollination and mosquito control. Owl boxes were also added to support natural rodent control.The Gottenborgs’ conservation work has not been limited to Eagle Rock Ranch. According to the Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust , Dave Gottenborg initiated discussions that eventually produced the nation’s first elk migration agreement.The voluntary programme was developed with the Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust and the Property and Environment Research Center. It uses private funding and incentives to compensate landowners who allow elk and other hoofed animals to move across their properties.The arrangement has since attracted interest among cattle ranchers and other landowners across the American West. Eagle Rock Ranch also hosts research into elk and deer crossings along county roads and highways. Working with the Property and Environment Research Center, researchers use trail-camera data to examine whether wildlife-friendly fencing can encourage elk to cross roads at safer, designated locations.The Gottenborgs have also taken steps to understand the range of life already present on their property. The Sand County Foundation reports that Dave invited the Colorado Natural Heritage Program to survey and catalogue the plants, birds and invertebrates found across the ranch.Instead of focusing only on cattle, fields or individual wildlife species, the survey looks at the wider biological community sharing the landscape.The changes have also supported the ranch’s economic side. Their daughter, Erin Michalski, returned to the family business after working as a Wall Street investment banker. She took responsibility for finishing, processing and marketing beef sold through the ranch’s retail shop and online.On 20 April 2026, the Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust announced that Eagle Rock Ranch had been selected for the 2026 Colorado Leopold Conservation Award. The award recognises farmers, ranchers and forestland owners who make significant efforts to improve soil health, water quality and wildlife habitat while managing working land.Dave and Jeannie Gottenborg received the award at the Colorado Cattlemen’s Association’s annual convention in June, along with a $10,000 prize. A property once marked by damaged fences, degraded vegetation, muddy corrals and stressed waterways has been reshaped through changes made over many years.
Article Summary: Eagle Rock Ranch in Colorado’s Park County has undergone a major transformation since Dave and Jeannie Gottenborg took ownership of the property. The couple began repairing the land while continuing to run cattle, gradually changing how the ranch handled water, grazing, vegetation and wildlife. Their work has now earned Eagle Rock Ranch the 2026 Colorado Leopold Conservation Award.

Article Title: At least 13 dead in suicide bomb blast near police post in northwestern Pakistan
Article Text:
Also Read:

Pakistani Taliban claims responsibility

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most important action the government should take in response to the recent attack? Increase security at checkpoints Strengthen military operations Enhance community awareness programs Focus on diplomacy with militant groups 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With AP inputs)

At least 13 people were killed and around 35 others wounded on Saturday when a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a roadside police checkpoint in northwestern Pakistan, police and rescue officials said.The attack took place in Dera Ismail Khan, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Local police chief Safdar Baloch said most of the injured were security personnel and passersby, with some in critical condition.According to Baloch, gunmen later opened fire on an ambulance carrying victims to a nearby hospital, killing a rescue worker and injuring two others.Two women and a child were also among those killed in the suicide bombing, he added.The Pakistan i Taliban, or Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), claimed responsibility for the attack. The TTP is separate from, but allied with, the Afghan Taliban, which returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021 after the US withdrew its troops.Pakistan has witnessed a surge in militant attacks in recent years, many of them claimed by the TTP and the outlawed Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a separatist group primarily active in neighbouring Balochistan province.Islamabad has repeatedly accused the Afghan Taliban of allowing TTP members to operate from Afghan soil and have demanded that Kabul prevent cross-border attacks into Pakistan. Afghan authorities have denied allowing their territory to be used for attacks against other countries.Dera Ismail Khan is near South Waziristan, a former militant stronghold where the Pakistani military has carried out several operations in recent years.In December 2023, a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at the main gate of a police station in Dera Ismail Khan, killing at least 23 security personnel in one of the deadliest attacks in the area. It was claimed by Tehreek-e-Jihad Pakistan, a small militant group believed to be an offshoot of the TTP.
Article Summary: The attack took place in Dera Ismail Khan, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The Pakistan i Taliban, or Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), claimed responsibility. The TTP is separate from, but allied with, the Afghan Taliban.

Article Title: Pakistan govt puts Islamabad on lockdown as Imran Khan’s party pushes ahead with march
Article Text:
Islamabad locked down as PTI prepares for Imran Khan march

Leaders of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party have vowed to press ahead with nationwide demonstrations demanding his release, as authorities tightened security in Islamabad ahead of the planned march.More than 1,000 shipping containers, many reinforced with spikes, have been placed to block roads, while sandbags have been positioned on bridges and a key highway leading into the capital has been closed. Public gatherings have also been banned in Islamabad, with 22,000 police and other security personnel deployed across the city.The government has also deployed security personnel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and closed the main highway linking the provincial capital, Peshawar, with Islamabad. The sweeping security measures have fuelled anger and frustration in the capital, with several businesses struggling to receive supplies.The measures to prevent Khan’s PTI from proceeding with the march come amid mounting concerns over the treatment of the former prime minister, who has been in jail since August 2023 following convictions in multiple cases.On Friday, PTI leaders announced that they would postpone the start of the march to October 4, a week after the original September 27 date, saying they hoped the delay would put further pressure on the government.The planned protest also comes amid the detention of three of Imran Khan’s sisters. Aleema Khan was detained last week, followed by Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, who were ordered to remain in custody for 30 days under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance.
Article Summary: More than 1,000 shipping containers, many reinforced with spikes, have been placed to block roads. Sandbags have been positioned on bridges and a key highway leading into the capital has been closed. Public gatherings have also been banned in Islamabad, with 22,000 police and other security personnel deployed.

Article Title: Pakistan goes bananas over giant gorillas dancing to Bollywood songs
Article Text:
Clips of these larger-than-life performers have been spreading rapidly online (Photo: AFP)

Pakistanis are going bananas over a trend that has crossed the Indian border: Giant gorillas, dancing to Bollywood music.Clips of these larger-than-life performers have been spreading rapidly online, turning them into the surprise stars of weddings, birthdays and other festivities.In the videos, guests can be seen joining in alongside the costumed entertainers, many of them visibly delighted by the unusual addition to their celebrations. The performers swing their oversized arms to pounding DJ tracks while partygoers gather round and dance, creating a lively, comic spectacle that has quickly drawn attention across social media.Behind the trend in Lahore is Shayen Zahoor, who runs Gorilla.co.pk, a business offering giant dancing gorilla acts for events across the city.Speaking to AFP, Zahoor explained how quickly the idea took off. He said the costume was ordered in early April and arrived by the end of the same month, after which the team wasted no time putting it to use.Once the suit arrived, he and his team lost no time getting started."We uploaded a reel on Instagram, and within just two days it reached a million views," Zahoor recalled.The overwhelming response convinced them to treat the venture as a serious business, and bookings soon began pouring in, with the public reaction proving remarkably enthusiastic."On the very first day, we received approximately 1,200 to 1,300 messages," he said, describing how curious would-be customers flooded his inbox.Many wanted to know whether the costume had genuinely arrived, what it would cost to book, and other practical details before making up their minds.What began as a single Instagram reel has since snowballed into a full-fledged entertainment phenomenon, with giant gorillas now a familiar, if unlikely, fixture at Pakistani celebrations.
Article Summary: Giant dancing gorillas have become a popular feature at Pakistani celebrations. The performers swing their oversized arms to pounding DJ tracks while partygoers gather round. A single Instagram reel has since snowballed into a full-fledged entertainment phenomenon. The trend has even crossed the Indian border.

Article Title: Pakistan govt crackdown forces PTI retreat? Imran's party likely to postpone Sept 27 Islamabad march
Article Text:
Imran Khan has been in jail since 2023

Pakistan minister says PTI has 'run away'

(With PTI inputs)

The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has decided to postpone its planned march to Islamabad from September 27 to October 4, party insiders said on Friday.The PTI had planned the march to the capital to demand the release of its incarcerated founder and former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan . The decision to delay the protest apparently came in response to the tough measures taken by the federal government to prevent it.According to PTI sources, the decision was taken at a party meeting and will be formally announced by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister and PTI leader Sohail Afridi.Earlier in the day, Afridi had asserted at a press conference in Peshawar that the planned long march would go ahead despite road blockades and other measures. However, he expressed concern over reports of nails being driven into roads at the provincial boundaries, questioning whether a conspiracy to “cut” Khyber Pakhtunkhwa off from the rest of Pakistan had formally begun.“Our long march will definitely take place. This time, we will definitely come out. Put nails on the roads, place containers or fire bullets, we will come out. We will end this corrupt system of fake rulers,” he told reporters.“Pakistan will not break at any cost and we will save Pakistan,” he added.Cricketer-turned-politician Khan, 73, has been held at Rawalpindi’s high-security Adiala Jail since 2023, when he was arrested following his conviction in a corruption case.Pakistan information minister Ataullah Tarar reacted to the reports by saying the PTI had “run away” because it had made “no preparations” for the march to Islamabad.“There are no preparations for the PTI’s long march either, and that is why they have backed out of this protest. If they have the courage, let them come and hold the march,” Tarar said.The federal government had placed shipping containers along Islamabad’s main roads, allowing them to be closed at short notice ahead of the planned march.Hotels in the Faizabad area of Rawalpindi had been closed, while restaurants and shopkeepers were directed to shut their businesses. Guest houses and transport terminals in Faizabad had also been ordered to close from Friday night.Thousands of security personnel were deployed in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, the capital’s twin city and home to Pakistan Army headquarters, to control Khan’s supporters.Tensions over the planned protest continued despite PTI chairman Gohar Ali Khan urging the government to open negotiations and warning against confronting political workers with force.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has decided to postpone its planned march to Islamabad from September 27 to October 4. The PTI had planned the march to the capital to demand the release of its founder and former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan. Khan has been held at Rawalpindi’s high-security Adiala Jail since 2023, when he was arrested following his conviction in a corruption case.

Article Title: 'Could endanger his life': Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest
Article Text:
Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest

Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan 's son Kasim Khan has urged Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) supporters not to march towards Rawalpindi's Adiala jail during the party's planned September 27 protest, warning that such a move could be used by Pakistani authorities as a pretext for a "counter" assault on the prison and put his father's life at risk.The warning comes ahead of the PTI's planned protest and march, which is being held to demand Imran Khan's release.The former premier has been in prison since August 2023 following convictions in multiple cases.In a post on X, Kasim said he had been asked to appeal to supporters against gathering near Adiala jail."I’ve been instructed to call on the public not to attempt to march or protest nearby Adiala jail on 27. I’ve heard from sources that this may be used as an excuse for the establishment to launch a “counter” assault on the jail (Which my father is being held in), which could endanger his life. Please do not give them any reasons for “accidents” to happen to my father during the protest," Kasim's post read.His appeal comes as security measures have been stepped up across Punjab ahead of the PTI mobilisation.The Punjab government has imposed Section 144 across the province from September 23 to October 5, restricting public gatherings of five or more people on roads and in public places. Authorities have also sought the deployment of Pakistan Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali.The restrictions have been imposed citing security concerns. A provincial notification referred to a "serious and imminent threat" to public peace and safety from militant and terrorist organisations and hostile intelligence agencies.The planned protest comes amid the detention of three of Imran Khan's sisters. Aleema Khan was detained last week, followed by Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, who were detained for 30 days under the Punjab maintenance of public order ordinance.On Thursday, the Lahore high court refused to immediately suspend the detention orders against Uzma and Noreen. The court issued notices to the respondents and sought their replies before taking up the plea further.The detentions have added to tensions ahead of the September 27 mobilisation.According to Dawn, lawyers for Uzma and Noreen told the Lahore high court that the two women were "non-political" and had been detained without sufficient legal justification. The court decided to wait for the authorities' response before ruling on their request to suspend the detention orders.Kasim had earlier criticised the detention of his aunts and other relatives and called for international attention to the issue.“This is a disgrace. Now my Aunts Dr. Uzma and Noreen, along with my cousins Shershah and Shahrez, have now been abducted as well. They have broken into my aunties' and cousins' houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation. No reasons for arrest have been stated," he said in a post on X.Pakistani authorities have said the preventive detentions and restrictions are linked to public-order and security concerns. The Punjab government's notification specifically cited threats from militant organisations and other security risks while announcing the province-wide restrictions.The September 27 PTI protest is expected to add to the political and security pressure surrounding Imran Khan's continued incarceration, with authorities tightening restrictions and increasing security in areas linked to the planned mobilisation.
Article Summary: Kasim Khan urges supporters not to march towards Rawalpindi's Adiala jail during the party's planned September 27 protest. He warns that such a move could be used as a pretext for a "counter" assault on the prison and put his father's life at risk. Security measures have been stepped up across Punjab ahead of the protest.

Article Title: Watch: Pakistan PM runs away from questions on Hafeez Saeed at UN
Article Text:
Pak PM skips questions at UN

Hafiz Saeed named in terror cases

India hits out at Pakistan at UN

Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday declined to answer questions from reporters about Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder Hafiz Saeed during his visit to the United Nations headquarters for the 81st UN General Assembly.As Sharif entered the UN headquarters, reporters asked him, “Prime Minister, when will you stop harbouring terrorists?” Sharif did not respond. Later, as he left the premises, he was again asked when Pakistan would prosecute Saeed, but the prime minister once again declined to answer.Hafiz Muhammad Saeed, founder of the proscribed LeT, is a designated terrorist under India's Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and is wanted as an accused in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attack case.The National Investigation Agency has also named Saeed as an accused in its supplementary chargesheet in the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack case. The NIA has alleged that Pakistan-based LeT operatives were involved in the attack and has named Saeed as Accused No. 8 in the alleged larger conspiracy.A day earlier, India criticised Pakistan at the United Nations, accusing Islamabad of focusing on territorial claims and cross-border terrorism instead of addressing its economic and domestic challenges.Exercising India's right of reply at the UN Human Rights Council, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi said Pakistan should focus on development rather than “coveting territory of others or exporting terror”.Tyagi also accused Pakistan of suppressing civilians in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and referred to reports of deaths, arrests and restrictions on essential supplies including food, fuel and medicine.
